description: The shape of a log line. Pino on the reference path, spdlog on the fast path, one JSON format. A disagreement between the two is a bug, which is why this is a contract and not a per-implementation setting.
principle: A log line is a structured event with a human sentence attached, not a sentence with fields attached. Tests compare the structure. The sentence is never compared — contracting English prose in two languages achieves nothing and cannot be kept green.
notCopiedFromLegacy: Legacy derives a log4js category per class and per method — 'backend.auth.jwt.JWT.verifyAndDecrypt' is a category. That taxonomy restates the file tree and grows with it. Here the category is a small closed set and the identity of a line is its event id.

envelope.description: Fields every line carries. time, level and msg keep Pino's default names so the reference path needs no custom serializer and the fast path has a fixed target to match.

fields.name: time
fields.description: UTC, see types/Timestamp.json. Pino's default already emits exactly this.

fields.name: event
fields.description: Stable dotted id. This is what tests assert on.

fields.name: msg
fields.description: One human sentence, present tense, no trailing period. Never compared between implementations, never parsed by anything.

fields.name: req
fields.description: Request correlation id. Present on every line emitted while serving a request.

fields.name: usr
fields.description: users.id, never the email and never the gradido_id.

fields.name: err
fields.description: Present when the line reports a failure: { code, name } from contracts/errors.

fields.name: data
fields.description: Event-specific fields, flat, no nesting beyond one level.

rules: No other top-level fields. Anything event-specific goes inside data.
Pino's default base fields pid and hostname must be disabled (base: null). They differ per process and would make two identical runs compare unequal.
No field is ever omitted for being empty except the ones marked optional, and an optional field is absent rather than null.

levels.description: Pino's numeric values. spdlog maps its own levels onto these numbers on output — the number is the contract, the spelling is not.

values.name: warn
values.use: recovered, but someone should know — e.g. an unknown role string from the database

categories.description: Closed set. It reuses the domain vocabulary from AGENTS.md rather than inventing a second taxonomy, so a category is a place in the system, not a place in the source tree. Adding one is a contract change.

values.name: mail
values.description: outbound mail: the session to the relay, and what was sent through it

rules: Lowercase, dot separated, no verbs in the past tense beyond the outcome.
The outcome is the last segment: created, failed, denied, refused, expired, evicted, refreshed, reverted, started, stopped, applied.
An event id never changes once it exists — see AGENTS.md, names are stable forever. To retire one, stop emitting it; do not rename it.
One event id means one shape: the same keys in data every time it is emitted, on both paths.

events.description: Seed set. This grows with the rebuild — an event is contracted when the code that emits it is written, not before.

values.note: The one line where the two implementations may legitimately differ in content: impl says which one is speaking.
The last line of a clean shutdown: connections stopped, database closed, log flushed.
The process exits with 1 after this line. timeout means the shutdown outlived its deadline and was cut short, so what it was waiting for did not finish.
The database did not answer, or answered that it will not: wrong credentials, no such database, no permission. The process exits with 1 after this line.

The process exits with 1 after this line. Distinct from startup.database.failed on purpose: the database answered, what is missing is a setup step nobody has taken — this instance has no community yet and there was no way to ask for one. See db/communities.json.

data.name: reason
data.description: closed vocabulary: unknown_contact, wrong_password, not_verified, deleted

values.note: Never log which of these it was to the client — the response says only that the login failed. The log may be specific; the response may not.
The ignore_and_warn policy of types/RoleNames.json is this line. Both implementations must emit it for the same input.
Hard timeout, SESSION_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS.

data.name: capacity
data.description: The configured maximum number of sessions -- the ceiling that was hit, not the number of slots in use.

values.note: The session store reached the ceiling it is configured with and retired its oldest session before that session's hard timeout. The owner's next request is a miss, a signature verification and a fresh session, so this is not an error -- it is the one signal that the store was not allowed to grow to the load it actually has, and warn rather than debug because nobody goes looking for it. Below the ceiling the store grows instead and this line never appears.
Carries err. The path is the route pattern, not the concrete URL — a concrete one leaks ids into the log.

data.name: attempt
data.description: One-based, so attempt 1 is the first try.

data.name: attempts
data.description: How many tries there will be in total.

values.note: One line per failed attempt while waiting for the database at startup. warn, not error: a database that is still starting up is expected, and the line that says it never came is startup.database.failed. The driver's own message goes in msg -- it is not a contracted error code, and it must never carry the connection password.
Carries err. Never the statement text and never the parameters.

data.name: version
data.description: The migration number, which becomes the schema version.

data.name: file
data.description: The migration name, so a line points at something findable.

values.note: One line per migration actually applied, at startup. Nothing is logged when the schema is already current: a line per boot saying that nothing changed teaches people to stop reading the log.

The migration was rolled back in full before this line — both target databases roll DDL back. The process then ends through startup.database.failed, so this line says which step failed and that one says the run is over.

data.name: url
data.description: Base URL other communities reach it at.

values.note: Written once, at the first start against a database that has no community. The key pair generated with it is never logged, in whole or in part — see redaction. This is the line an admin looks for when they want to know when the instance was set up.

data.name: version
data.description: The migration that was undone. The database is now at version - 1.

values.note: One down step, and only ever one per run. warn rather than info because a down step is not the inverse of an up step — what it dropped, it dropped with its rows. On a release the run had to be confirmed by naming this migration; how that confirmation is given is each implementation's own business, that it is required is not.

A down run that did not happen: unconfirmed on a release, confirmed with the wrong name, nothing applied, or a migration with no down step. Which of those is in msg rather than in a field, the way db.connection.failed carries the driver's own message — the process exits with 1 and a person reads the line. Distinct from db.migration.denied, which is about a schema this build cannot run against at all and names where it diverges.

data.name: version
data.description: The applied migration this build cannot account for.

data.name: file
data.description: Its name, as the database recorded it.

data.name: expected
data.description: What this build has at that version, or null when the database is simply ahead.

values.note: The database was built by code this build is not, so nothing is applied and the process exits. msg names the migration to go back past and says the branch that applied it is where the down step lives — this one has no down step for a migration it does not have. Distinct from db.migration.failed, where a migration this build does carry was rolled back.

data.name: language
data.description: The Language enum value the account was created with.

values.note: Carries usr with the new users.id. Never the email address — the account is identifiable without carrying personal data into log storage, see redaction.

A registration that was answered as if it had succeeded. Carries usr with the id of the member who already holds the address — not of anybody new, because none was created. The answer to the caller says nothing about this; the log is the only place it is visible, which is the point.

redaction.description: Never logged, at any level, in either implementation. Not a policy that can be relaxed by configuration.

never.why: the PHC string carries the salt and the full hash
possession of it is proof of the email

never.what: JWTs, in whole or in part
never.why: a token in a log is a token in every backup of that log
use usr with users.id — the account is identifiable without carrying personal data into log storage

never.what: avatar bytes and any other blob

never.why: it is user input and frequently an email

never.what: concrete request URLs with ids in the path
never.why: log the route pattern; the id belongs in data if it is needed at all

comparison.description: How a contract test decides that both implementations logged the same thing.
rules: Compare: level, cat, event, presence and value of every data key, and err.code when present.
Ignore: msg, time, req, and field order.
A missing event on the fast path is a documented gap, the same as a skipped contract test — not a failure to hide by loosening the comparison.
